title: 第三块石板下面  (Under the Third Stone)

segments.t: At ten o'clock Friday night, Qing, Chen, and Manager Zhou gather under the warm front-desk lamp as Qing turns over the thick stamped postcard from the gate mailbox. Listen first.
快看两个星期前的邮戳！谁会从国外给小院客栈写信呢？
你们听：“亲爱的小院朋友们，三十年前的五月，我住过八号房！”
三十年前的五月——正好是下大雨的那个星期！小晴，接着往下念。
“那时我是个年轻的制图员，你们阳光房的热茶救了我淋湿的地图。”
八号房！让我查查我姑姑的绿登记本——对，这位制图员就在这儿！
继续听：“出远门回家以前，我和您姑姑藏了一个小铁盒时间胶囊。”
时间胶囊？！在我自己的小院里？！
小晴，那位制图员写他们藏在哪儿了吗？
“如果你们有一天重开九号房，从老树往北数三块平石板！”
从老树往北数三块平石板？！那就在一号桌正底下呀！
等等——傍晚我垫平一号桌的时候，第三块石板敲起来是空的！
两位先生，快提上灯笼——九号房开张了，下一个谜团就在树底下！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
快看两个星期前的邮戳！谁会从国外给小院客栈写信呢？

'Look at the postmark from two weeks ago! Who writes to Courtyard Inn from abroad?' "Guowai" literally says "country-outside" for "abroad", and "gei... xie xin" puts "to Courtyard Inn" ahead of "write a letter".
你们听：“亲爱的小院朋友们，三十年前的五月，我住过八号房！”
'Listen to this: "Dear courtyard friends, thirty years ago this May I stayed in Room Eight!"' Soft "guo" right after "zhu", "stay", marks a cherished life experience—"I once stayed in Room Eight".
三十年前的五月——正好是下大雨的那个星期！小晴，接着往下念。

'Thirty years ago this May—that exact rainy week! Read the rest, Qing.' "Wang xia nian" literally says "read aloud downward" along the page, while "nian" specifically means reading words out loud rather than silently.
“那时我是个年轻的制图员，你们阳光房的热茶救了我淋湿的地图。”

'"I was a young mapmaker, and your sunroom tea saved my wet maps."' See how "zhituyuan" clicks together: "make" plus "map" plus "-yuan" for a specialist, echoed right beside "ditu", "earth-chart", for map.
八号房！让我查查我姑姑的绿登记本——对，这位制图员就在这儿！

'Room Eight! Let me check my aunt's green guest book—yes, the mapmaker is right here!' "Chacha"—doubling "cha", "look up"—is the quick everyday word for flipping through a ledger, dictionary, or guest list.
继续听：“出远门回家以前，我和您姑姑藏了一个小铁盒时间胶囊。”

'Keep listening: "Before my long journey home, your aunt and I hid a small tin time capsule."' "Chu yuanmen" literally says "go out the far door"—setting off on a long journey—and Mandarin naturally puts "I" first in "wo he nin gugu", "I and your aunt".
时间胶囊？！在我自己的小院里？！
'A time capsule?! In my own courtyard?!' Pairing "wo" with "ziji"—"my own"—captures Manager Zhou's comic astonishment that a secret sat under his shoes for fifteen years.
小晴，那位制图员写他们藏在哪儿了吗？
'Does the mapmaker say where they hid it, Qing?' "Cang zai nar", literally "hid at where", keeps normal Mandarin order even inside "did they write where they hid it?".
“如果你们有一天重开九号房，从老树往北数三块平石板！”

'"If you ever reopen Room Nine, count three flat stones north from the old tree!"' Watch that versatile character "chong" in "chong kai", "re-open": read "chong" it means "again", whereas read "zhong" it means "heavy".
从老树往北数三块平石板？！那就在一号桌正底下呀！
'Three flat stones north from the tree?! That is right under table number one!' Putting "zheng" right before "dixia", "underneath", sharpens it into "dead underneath"—spot on the mark.
等等——傍晚我垫平一号桌的时候，第三块石板敲起来是空的！

'Hold on—when I levelled table one at dusk, that third stone sounded hollow!' Adding "qilai" after an action like "tap", "listen", or "taste" is how Mandarin says "when you tap it, it sounds..."—here "kong de", hollow!
两位先生，快提上灯笼——九号房开张了，下一个谜团就在树底下！

'Grab the lantern, gentlemen—Room Nine is open, and our next mystery starts under the tree!' "Ti" specifically means carrying something dangling from a handle like a lantern or basket, and celebratory "kaizhang" means a café or shop officially opening its doors!
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

Room Nine is open, the courtyard café is thriving, and under the third stone from the old shade tree waits a thirty-year-old time capsule as Season 2 of Courtyard Inn comes to a close! See you next time.
下次见！
